batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 distinct candidate IDs and their supplied premeasurement V1/V2 predictions. Combine condition-response measurements in historically failure-prone regions with controlled loading contrasts and focused structural transfer tests. Prioritize relationships that can inform many catalog rows; use quantile widths only as secondary evidence because they are not calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

choices.reason: m160 at 1/1 and 100 ul predicts 6.60/24.63 mL. It completes a fixed-loading curve with measured 2/1 and 5/1 rows 2feb7d8e0a3566ddf97f and b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90, whose endpoints increased sharply. This locates the stronger-eluent side of the amino-nitrile response.

m66 at 2/1 predicts 14.58/31.32 mL, including completion earlier than the measured 1/1 value of 34.83 mL in 8f5acbec0c511bb1ea89. At identical loading, this tests a possible misplaced response shape between the measured pure-EA and 1/1 anchors and the selected 5/1 point.

The matched m66 5/1 experiment predicts 27.89/64.25 mL. Together with the selected 2/1 point and measured 07dbb8c9982caa472c1a and 8f5acbec0c511bb1ea89, it tests whether the pyridyl ketone develops the predicted steep completion response as EA fraction decreases.

m146 at 10/1 and 100 ul predicts 31.16/60.41 mL, almost unchanged from measured 5/1 endpoints 31.31/60.95 in 51f5ae6a991eea9e720e. This fixed-loading extension distinguishes a real plateau from an insufficiently learned weak-eluent response for the methylquinoline scaffold.

m125 at 5/1, 50 mg and 300 ul DCM predicts 36.09/68.16 mL. With the selected 500 ul counterpart, it completes an amount-by-loading-volume comparison against measured 100 mg rows 74cf50c6ec476a394b01 and c4b5a5499258f39b7ac1.

Change only m125 DCM loading volume from 300 to 500 ul at 5/1 and 50 mg; predictions remain 36.09/68.16 mL. Measurements can test whether the volume effect depends on amount, following the different volume relationships observed at 2/1 and 5/1.

m177 at 50/1 and 70.3 mg predicts 7.73/46.10 mL. This starts a controlled amount pair extending the measured 20/1 contrast aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58 versus 5e276c1730fc0a9deba7, where completion differed greatly while onset remained early.

The matched m177 50/1 experiment raises sample amount to 210.9 mg while retaining 1000 ul DCM loading volume. Its prediction, 7.73/46.11 mL, is essentially unchanged. This tests whether the amount-dependent completion pattern seen at 5/1 and 20/1 extends into weaker eluent.

Cinnamic acid m173 at 2/1 with 1500 ul DCM predicts 7.68/30.59 mL and starts a fixed-loading pair with 10/1. Measured 1e775e7d8dcbf48fd6f8 exposed substantial historical V2 underprediction at 5/1; its 2000 ul loading volume remains an explicit comparison difference.

The matched m173 10/1 point predicts 21.81/82.76 mL. The two selected labels determine an acid response over a substantial solvent-strength range and test whether completion and onset require different condition dependencies after the recent 5/1 correction.

m99 at 5/1 and 150 ul predicts 20.43/33.35 mL. Comparison with measured 100 ul row 12ab195583f05b9aa177 tests amount transfer in the hydroxy-ester environment and supplies the loading-matched baseline for the selected 10/1 experiment.

At unchanged 150 ul sample volume and 1000 ul DCM loading volume, m99 at 10/1 predicts 18.91/35.88 mL. This challenges the predicted slight decrease in onset and nearly flat completion from 5/1, without assuming that all alcohol-containing compounds must share a monotone response.
m119 at 5/1 and 150 ul predicts 33.46/67.07 mL. It extends measured 1/1 row c32caf65e93924aeb179 at identical loading and tests the steep response assigned to a methoxy-substituted phenethyl alcohol.

Related methoxybenzyl alcohol m120 at 5/1 and 150 ul predicts 20.95/49.66 mL. Alongside m119, it tests the predicted attachment-dependent contrast suggested by naphthyl alcohol observations 48853fd78c77153b963a and 614873124b33029a924c. Density-derived amounts differ between structures.

Novel methyl acetoacetate m95 at 2/1 and 50 ul predicts 8.17/21.37 mL. It anchors a matched 20/1 test and probes transfer from ethyl acetoacetate observations 7a3586b45c03832259f5 and ce539fc06bdda7c0ed0d into a closely related beta-keto ester.

The matched m95 20/1 point predicts 12.26/19.97 mL: later onset but slightly earlier completion than at 2/1. These labels test the predicted flat V2 response over a large decrease in EA fraction, a useful contrast to the steep measured m13 curve.

Novel ether-containing beta-keto ester m107 at 2/1 and 100 ul predicts 8.37/23.45 mL. This begins a fixed-loading pair that tests transfer between simpler acetoacetates and the multifunctional m13 failure region.

At unchanged loading, m107 at 5/1 predicts 18.37/33.44 mL. Together with its selected 2/1 label, it determines whether the added ether environment has the predicted response. Cross-molecule comparisons with m95 will retain their amount differences.

Novel tetralone m180 at 5/1 predicts 8.40/18.06 mL and starts a matched 50/1 pair. Its high structural similarity to observed cyclic ketones makes this a focused test of ring-environment transfer, with m63 and m179 providing neighboring scaffold contexts.

The matched m180 50/1 point predicts 21.98/44.71 mL. Measuring both conditions distinguishes a scaffold offset from an incorrect solvent-response slope and can improve transfer across cyclic aromatic ketones represented by 87727a0338c26706a350 and 8b8becd233748ccae9e3.

Novel m106, an ether-chain aromatic ketone with maximum observed similarity 0.390, predicts ordinary endpoints of 5.81/9.60 mL at 2/1. It starts a matched response pair in a joint chain, ether and fluorinated-aromatic environment absent from the measured set.

The matched m106 20/1 point predicts 15.45/28.91 mL. Its label tests whether the predicted solvent sensitivity transfers from simpler aromatic ketones and ether-containing compounds, while the pair isolates mobile-phase response within this new structure.

Novel aliphatic chloroketone m27 at 2/1 and 150 ul predicts 8.05/12.44 mL. Its maximum observed similarity is 0.276. The label extends ketone coverage beyond predominantly aromatic environments and anchors the selected 20/1 experiment.

At identical loading, m27 at 20/1 predicts 15.86/28.29 mL. This tests the substantial response assigned to a compact single-carbonyl aliphatic structure; observed aromatic chloroketone 067c1cac53731e589c4b offers a related, chemically distinct reference.

Novel naphthylacetate ester m98 at 5/1 and 50 ul predicts 13.35/24.07 mL. It tests donor-free retention transfer in a naphthyl family where alcohol rows 48853fd78c77153b963a and 614873124b33029a924c showed substantial retention, with their loading differences kept explicit.

The matched m98 20/1 point predicts 17.54/29.73 mL. This tests its relatively shallow predicted response and helps distinguish transferable naphthyl effects from functional-group-specific solvent sensitivity.

Novel 2,6-difluorobenzaldehyde m185 at 20/1 predicts 12.71/25.60 mL. It tests transfer into an ortho-fluorinated carbonyl environment and the substantial contrast predicted against the selected m187 aldehyde under the same nominal sample volume and loading solvent conditions.

Novel bromo-trifluoromethyl benzaldehyde m187 at 20/1 predicts 5.54/15.20 mL. Together with m185, it tests whether the model's large substitution-dependent contrast is supported. Their density-derived amounts differ, so the comparison informs the joint structure-condition mapping.

Novel conjugated dienone m164 at 5/1 predicts 6.32/17.01 mL and starts a fixed-loading 20/1 pair. It tests transfer from the chalcone environment represented by measured 0bdd638e906bf11a00cb into a more extended conjugated carbonyl structure.

The matched m164 20/1 point predicts 12.86/33.69 mL. The pair measures the response of an extended, donor-free aromatic carbonyl and provides a neutral structural-transfer test alongside the nitrogen, acid and loading-focused measurements.

m128 at 10/1 and 100 ul predicts 19.02/39.81 mL. The methylthio ketone had substantial historical underprediction in 91cd087e44e7a3364533 at 5/1 and 150 ul. This extension tests the revised mapping; the sample-amount difference prevents treating it as a pure solvent contrast with that observation.

m129 at 10/1 predicts 15.26/29.60 mL and exactly matches the loading of measured 5/1 row cf8ab33c25ad391a584c. It establishes an aldehyde response and tests whether the ketone-versus-aldehyde contrast revealed last round persists at another mobile-phase ratio.

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen environment and mobile-phase composition jointly determine response shape and completion behavior. The model may still misplace the transition to later retention in pyridyl carbonyls or infer a premature plateau for methylquinoline; a common nitrogen-family correction would be insufficient.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These families produced different acquisition-time error patterns. Additional condition anchors can teach structure-by-solvent interactions and separate onset from completion corrections.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m66 follow the predicted 2/1-to-5/1 transition, does m146 plateau from 5/1 to 10/1, and does m160's stronger-eluent anchor fit its measured steep response?

hypotheses.content: The predictor's near-invariance to loading variables is inadequate in some recorded structure-condition regions. Loading relationships appear dependent on scaffold and mobile-phase ratio; the observations do not support a universal direction for the effect of DCM loading volume.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controlled contrasts can reveal interactions missing from the density-times-volume and loading-volume features. They can also show where observed variation remains insufficiently explained by the recorded variables.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 5/1, does m125's loading-volume relationship change between 50 and 100 mg? At 50/1, does m177 completion differ between 70.3 and 210.9 mg despite nearly identical predictions?

hypotheses.content: Hydroxyl attachment and co-functional groups may give V1 and V2 different solvent dependencies. The nearly flat predicted m99 response, the methoxy phenethyl-versus-benzyl alcohol contrast, and the acid completion response require separate tests rather than a universal donor correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Recent donor-containing examples had errors in both directions, including completion failure with nearly correct onset. These measurements can improve transfer among alcohol, hydroxy-ester and acid environments while accounting for loading.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m99 remain almost unchanged from 5/1 to 10/1 at fixed loading, does the predicted m119/m120 contrast hold, and how steep is the matched cinnamic-acid response?

hypotheses.content: The steep measured response of multifunctional m13 need not transfer to all beta-keto esters. The model predicts an almost flat m95 completion response from 2/1 to 20/1 but a substantial m107 increase from 2/1 to 5/1; these are untested structural-transfer predictions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Related ester and carbonyl structures occupy many rows. Within-molecule response pairs can determine whether ether placement and carbonyl environment are being transferred appropriately, without attributing cross-molecule differences solely to acceptor count.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the separate fixed-loading curves support m95's predicted V2 plateau and m107's predicted rise, or do these structures require different condition-response corrections?

hypotheses.content: The earlier model's near-equality for methylthio aromatic ketone and aldehyde endpoints at 5/1 was not supported by the measured rows. Sulfur transfer may require carbonyl-type and solvent-strength interactions; differing sample amounts limit causal attribution of the observed structural contrast.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The ketone was historically underpredicted while the aldehyde was overpredicted. A shared sulfur offset would miss this distinction, and another condition can test whether the revised structural contrast generalizes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 10/1, does the ketone retain later completion than the aldehyde, and does the aldehyde's loading-matched 5/1-to-10/1 response agree with prediction?

feedback_interpretation: Last round strengthened the case for learning conditional responses rather than broad functional-group offsets. m160 showed a much steeper measured 2/1-to-5/1 response than anticipated, with acquisition-time V2 underprediction of 49.95 mL at 5/1, whereas dibenzylamine completion at 5/1 was close to prediction. m66 still finished at 21.09 mL in pure EA. The m125 results weakened a simple loading-volume interpretation: increasing DCM volume delayed both endpoints at the measured 2/1 low-amount contrast, but at 5/1 and 100 mg it advanced onset while completion changed little. m177 showed an amount-associated completion difference at both 5/1 and 20/1, with strongly different magnitudes; this motivates another controlled condition rather than a universal amount correction. The similar m205 endpoints at 100 and 150 ul further caution against generalizing large loading effects to every scaffold. The m13 curve was genuinely steep, but its 5/1 historical V2 prediction overshot by 20.01 mL; m39's response pair was much closer. Hydroxy ester and cinnamic acid labels exposed underprediction, while several ordinary alcohol predictions were high. Finally, methylthio ketone and aldehyde outcomes diverged substantially. These are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals. Current predictions already reflect retraining, so this batch tests remaining response shapes and transfer to related unmeasured structures.
batch_rationale: The 32 experiments cover 20 molecules. Fixed-loading solvent-response pairs provide interpretable local labels for pyridyl ketone, cinnamic acid, hydroxy ester, beta-keto esters, cyclic ketone, ether-chain ketone, aliphatic chloroketone, naphthyl ester and conjugated dienone environments. Extensions of measured amino-nitrile, methylquinoline, alcohol and sulfur-containing curves target relationships highlighted by feedback. The m125 and m177 contrasts specifically test loading interactions that the current predictions largely suppress. Nine previously unobserved molecules extend coverage through chemically meaningful neighbors and less similar carbonyl environments, including ordinary predicted endpoint ranges. The aldehyde substitution comparison and alcohol attachment comparison test particular structural distinctions, with density-derived amount and other loading differences retained in interpretation. This combination can improve generalization across the carbonyl-rich Row-distribution while repairing nitrogen, donor and loading relationships that previously failed. Repeated catalog tuples were not selected within this batch. Neither large predicted volumes nor V2 minus V1 served as an acquisition objective, and the elution interval was not treated as uncertainty.
